z-m-09-05.title: How far rule for adding odd numbers in order work?
z-m-09-05.topic: Range where sum rule holds (starting number)
z-m-09-05.goal: Use a pattern from few examples to predict, but see rule may change when starting number condition changes; adjust confidence.

z-m-09-05.thinking.0: Guessing far value with a rule

z-m-09-04.title: Planting trees along road at equal intervals
z-m-09-04.topic: Relationship between number of gaps and objects
z-m-09-04.goal: Learn gap count and tree count may differ; find missing info for decision and make several lengths/intervals that fit.
z-m-09-04.material: Straight road 20m long. Plant trees along one edge, equal intervals. Ignore tree thickness. Interval means distance between neighboring trees. Jisu say, 'If interval 4m, 20÷4=5, so need 5 trees!' 20 4 20 4 5 5
z-m-09-04.thinking.2: Saying how answer changes when condition changes
z-m-09-04.s.s1.prompt: To check Jisu's 5 trees, what must know first? 5
z-m-09-04.s.s1.hint.0: Draw road as line, mark tree spot every 4m. 4
z-m-09-04.s.s1.hint.1: Count gaps and compare with tree spots.
z-m-09-04.s.s1.r.a: Divisibility helps find gap count. Tree count depend what happens at endpoints.
z-m-09-04.s.s1.o.b: Whether trees also at first and last point
z-m-09-04.s.s1.r.b: Relationship of gaps and trees depend whether both endpoints get trees. You identify condition first.
z-m-09-04.s.s1.o.c: Whether 4m between trees measured trunk centers or edges 4
z-m-09-04.s.s1.r.c: Problem says ignore thickness. You challenge condition already set.
z-m-09-04.s.s1.r.d: Tree type not used to decide count.
z-m-09-04.s.s1.explain: With same 20m and 4m interval, trees at both endpoints give 6; at one endpoint gives 5; neither endpoint gives 4. Gaps always 5, but tree count depends endpoint condition. Jisu's 5 correct only when planting at one end. 20 4 6 5 4 5 5
z-m-09-04.s.s2.prompt: Now suppose trees at both endpoints too. Make 3 different roads with exactly 7 trees. Choose length L (m) and interval d (m). (L,d natural numbers; d from 1m to 10m; all gaps equal.) 3 7 1 10
z-m-09-04.s.s2.hint.0: Line up 7 trees and count gaps between neighbors. 7
z-m-09-04.s.s2.hint.1: Choose interval first, then length; mark dots to check exactly 7 fit. 7
z-m-09-04.s.s2.ok.c1: Interval natural number 1 to 10m; length natural too. 1 10
z-m-09-04.s.s2.fail.c1: Write interval natural 1 to 10 and length natural number. 1 10
z-m-09-04.s.s2.ok.c2: With this length and interval, exactly 7 trees. 7
z-m-09-04.s.s2.fail.c2: This length/interval won't give 7 trees. Count gaps. 7
z-m-09-04.s.s2.explain: With 7 trees at both ends, 6 gaps. Road length 6 times interval. (12m/2m, 30m/5m, 60m/10m, 6m/1m ...). Dividing length by interval gives gaps, no trees. 7 6 6 12 2 30 5 60 10 6 1
z-m-09-04.s.s3.prompt: If plant trees around circular pond perimeter 20m, every 4m, how many trees? Explain difference from straight road. 20 4
z-m-09-04.s.s3.hint.0: Draw pond perimeter as circle, choose start point, mark every 4m. 4
z-m-09-04.s.s3.hint.1: When you go around and return to start, do you count starting point again?

z-m-09-04.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You compare with reason straight road get 6? 6
z-m-09-04.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You say how first and last spots relate on pond?
z-m-09-04.s.s3.model.0: 5 trees. Round pond comes back to starting spot, so no separate endpoints; 5 gaps, 5 trees. 5 5 5
z-m-09-04.s.s3.model.1: 5 trees. Straight road start/end different, so one more tree than gaps; pond start=end, so tree/gap counts same. 5

z-m-09-01.title: How number of blocks for staircase dey grow?
z-m-09-01.topic: Patterns in number sequence wey increase amount dey change
z-m-09-01.goal: For number sequence wey increase no constant, find the problem with guess based on change for just one stretch; make your own sequence with same kind rule, and explain how to find term far ahead.
z-m-09-01.material: Minjae dey build staircase shape with blocks. Bottom row longest, and each row going up get 1 block less. 1st staircase get 1 block, 2nd get 3, 3rd get 6, and 4th get 10. Minjae talk, 'The 3rd get 6, wey na 3 more, so e go continue increase by 3 every time. The 5th staircase na 10+3=13 blocks!'
z-m-09-01.thinking.0: Compare all the changes, no be only one stretch
z-m-09-01.thinking.1: Make another example yourself with the same rule
z-m-09-01.thinking.2: Explain with words how to find a term far ahead
z-m-09-01.prereq.0: Find rules in number sequences (Grades 3-4 level)
z-m-09-01.s.s1.prompt: Look Minjae guess and choose the most fitting number of blocks for 5th staircase.
z-m-09-01.s.s1.hint.0: Write in order how many more blocks each staircase get than the one before am.
z-m-09-01.s.s1.hint.1: Put the increases side by side and compare whether dem same or how dem different.
z-m-09-01.s.s1.o.a: 13 blocks: think say e go increase by 3 each time
z-m-09-01.s.s1.r.a: Increase of 3 happen for one place only, from 2nd to 3rd. From 1st to 2nd e increase by 2, and from 3rd to 4th e increase by 4. First check whether increase stay constant.
z-m-09-01.s.s1.o.b: 14 blocks: think say last increase (4) go happen again
z-m-09-01.s.s1.r.b: This look only the last change and assume next one go be the same. If you put increases from beginning side by side, dem na 2, 3, 4, different each time.
z-m-09-01.s.s1.o.c: 15 blocks: think say increase go grow by one each time, like 2, 3, 4
z-m-09-01.s.s1.r.c: Na thinking wey notice say increases different from each other and see how dem change as rule.
z-m-09-01.s.s1.o.d: 20 blocks: think say previous number roughly double
z-m-09-01.s.s1.r.d: From 1 to 3 and 3 to 6, e almost double, but from 6 to 10 e less than double. Na judgment based only on few places wey look alike.
z-m-09-01.s.s1.explain: Blocks added for each staircase na 2, 3, 4, one more every time. If this change continue, next increase na 5, and 10+5=15 blocks. You get same answer if you think about staircase shape (new bottom row get as many blocks as its position number). If you look at change for one place only (3), like Minjae, e no fit other places.
z-m-09-01.s.s2.prompt: Minjae talk how e dey build staircase: 'I add one more row for bottom of previous staircase, and that row get 1 more block than row directly above am.' Sequence wey increase grow by 1 each time fit also happen if you change starting number. Make 3 different sequences with four numbers in order. (All na natural numbers, second number must pass first, and increase must grow by exactly 1 every time.)
z-m-09-01.s.s2.hint.0: First choose first number, then decide wetin the first increase go be.
z-m-09-01.s.s2.hint.1: Add the amount wey you decide to make second number, then decide each next increase by comparing with previous one, and write up to fourth number.
z-m-09-01.s.s2.ok.c1: All four numbers na natural numbers.
z-m-09-01.s.s2.fail.c1: Write all four numbers as natural numbers wey be 1 or more.
z-m-09-01.s.s2.ok.c3: Second increase na 1 more than first increase.
z-m-09-01.s.s2.fail.c3: Second increase must be exactly 1 more than first increase.
z-m-09-01.s.s2.ok.c4: Third increase na 1 more than second increase.
z-m-09-01.s.s2.fail.c4: Third increase must be exactly 1 more than second increase.
z-m-09-01.s.s2.explain: For example, (1, 3, 6, 10) increase by 2, 3, 4; (2, 3, 5, 8) and (5, 6, 8, 11) increase by 1, 2, 3. (3, 6, 10, 15) increase by 3, 4, 5. Even if starting number different, the rule 'increase grow by 1' same. (1, 3, 5, 7) get constant increase of 2, so e no meet this condition.
z-m-09-01.s.s3.prompt: For Minjae staircase (1, 3, 6, 10, …), how many blocks the 10th staircase get? Briefly write method wey you use. More than one method dey.
z-m-09-01.s.s3.hint.0: First think how many blocks bottom row for 10th staircase get.
z-m-09-01.s.s3.hint.1: Increase position one by one, like 5th, 6th, ..., and write the rule wey number dey grow by.
z-m-09-01.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You explain with your own words how the increase change?
z-m-09-01.s.s3.selfAssess.1: Your work show how you continue to 10th or calculate in another way?
z-m-09-01.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You compare whether your answer same as sample answer and how methods different?
z-m-09-01.s.s3.model.0: The increase grow as 2, 3, 4, 5, ..., so 5th na 15 blocks, 6th na 21, 7th na 28, 8th na 36, 9th na 45, and 10th na 55 blocks.
z-m-09-01.s.s3.model.1: 10th staircase get 10 blocks for bottom row, and each row going up get 1 less. So adding 10+9+8+…+1 give 55 blocks.
z-m-09-01.s.s3.model.2: If you pair numbers from 1 to 10, first and last, you get 5 pairs with total 11, so 55 blocks.

z-m-09-08.title: Fill bucket from tap: amount of water ahead
z-m-09-08.topic: Conditions to extend rule wey you find from measured data for prediction (rule continues, bucket limit)
z-m-09-08.goal: Wen you predict far-off value with rule so far, state the conditions wey make that value hold (same flow continues, bucket size), set in numbers the range wey rule hold, then say it together with the conditions.
z-m-09-08.material:
Sujin fill empty bucket with water from tap and measure water amount every minute (unit: L, liters). Tap stay running at same strength.
- 1 min: 4L
- 2 min: 8L
- 3 min: 12L
- 4 min: 16L
Bucket fit hold up to 30L water. Sujin talk, 'E increase by 4L every minute, so after 10 minutes e go get 4×10=40L!'
z-m-09-08.thinking.0: Notice conditions wey hide inside a rule
z-m-09-08.thinking.1: Set the range where rule hold
z-m-09-08.thinking.2: Honestly say prediction by naming its conditions

z-m-09-08.s.s1.hint.1: Write how wetin table show (up to 4 minutes) differ from wetin she wan talk (after 10 minutes).
z-m-09-08.s.s1.o.a: Table show 4L every minute, so after 10 minutes e go surely get 40L
z-m-09-08.s.s1.r.a: Na value wey you find by carrying the rule so far straight to 10 minutes. You no check whether that value fit really dey inside this bucket.
z-m-09-08.s.s1.o.b: We only measure up to 4 minutes, so we no fit guess water amount after 10 minutes at all
z-m-09-08.s.s1.r.b: You give up on guessing even though data dey. If you look the rule together with other information, one thing fit be said.
z-m-09-08.s.s1.o.c: Even if tap stay same strength, this bucket fit hold only up to 30L, so 40L no fit dey inside after 10 minutes
z-m-09-08.s.s1.r.c: You compare value from the rule with amount bucket fit hold.
z-m-09-08.s.s1.o.d: Water go come faster and faster, so after 10 minutes e go get more than 40L
z-m-09-08.s.s1.r.d: For table, amount wey increase each minute na the same. You make up a change wey no dey in table.
z-m-09-08.s.s1.explain: 4×10=40 na value wey you get by extending rule 'tap continue to run same strength' to 10 minutes. But bucket fit hold only 30L, so even if rule continue as e be, 40L no fit enter. You fit use table rule only within the range bucket fit hold.
z-m-09-08.s.s2.prompt: Think about time after 5 minutes, wey dem never measure. If tap continue same strength and water no overflow, write 2 different times m (minutes) wen bucket get 4×m L. (m na natural number 5 or more.)
z-m-09-08.s.s2.hint.0: Choose m, find 4×m, and compare with 30.

z-m-09-08.s.s2.ok.c2: E dey after 5 minutes, wey dem never measure yet.
z-m-09-08.s.s2.ok.c3: 4×m na 30 or less, so e fit inside bucket.
z-m-09-08.s.s2.fail.c3: If 4×m pass 30, no fit all enter bucket. Find 4×m and compare with 30.
z-m-09-08.s.s2.explain: 4×5=20, 4×6=24 and 4×7=28 na 30 or less, so dem fit. From 4×8=32 onward e pass 30 and bucket overflow. So rule fit use up to 7 minutes.
z-m-09-08.s.s3.prompt: One friend ask, 'About how many minutes until bucket full?' Answer honestly, include numbers and reason (condition) you use.
z-m-09-08.s.s3.hint.0: Write out amount wey add each minute after 5 minutes, then compare with 30L.
z-m-09-08.s.s3.hint.1: Find the minute wey e start to pass 30L, and write condition wey you need mention too.

z-m-09-02.title: Perimeter of tiles joined together: if expressions look different, na the same rule?
z-m-09-02.topic: Rules written as expressions: compare expressions wey look different
z-m-09-02.goal: Sort out expression wey correct for only one case, and explain by putting different values say expressions with different forms fit show same rule.
z-m-09-02.material:
Rectangular tile dey, 3 cm wide and 2 cm high. Put tiles in one row, join side by side with their 2 cm sides exactly touching. Perimeter of 1 tile na 10 cm. Join 2 and e make rectangle 6 cm wide and 2 cm high, perimeter 16 cm; join 3 and e make 9 cm wide and 2 cm high, perimeter 22 cm. You wan write total perimeter (cm) wen □ tiles join as expression using □. Four friends make expressions.
- Doyun: (3×□+2)×2
- Hajun: 10×□−2×(□−1)
- Mina: 6×□+4
- Seoha: 10×□−4×(□−1)

z-m-09-02.thinking.1: Find first line wey wrong for incorrect explanation
z-m-09-02.thinking.2: Use evidence explain wetin expressions with different forms get in common
z-m-09-02.prereq.0: Perimeter of rectangle (total length of all sides)
z-m-09-02.prereq.1: Put numbers inside expressions with □ to find value (expressions with multiplication, addition, subtraction and parentheses)

z-m-09-02.s.s1.r.d: Na method wey add all tile perimeters together then subtract the parts wey touch and dey inside.

z-m-09-03.title: Time table for Korea and Hanoi: the rule always same?
z-m-09-03.topic: Range wey a correspondence rule between two quantities hold
z-m-09-03.goal: Doubt whether rule wey work for few cases in table work for all cases; find a case where rule fail yourself, then rewrite the rule.
z-m-09-03.material:
You wan video call your aunt wey dey Hanoi (Vietnam). For this problem, Korea always 2 hours ahead of Hanoi. For clock, a day start midnight (12 a.m.). Your aunt send this time table.
- Wen na 10 a.m. for Korea, na 8 a.m. same day for Hanoi
- Wen na 3 p.m. for Korea, na 1 p.m. same day for Hanoi
- Wen na 9 p.m. for Korea, na 7 p.m. same day for Hanoi
Ayun talk, 'Time for Hanoi na time wey 2 hours earlier than Korea. E correct for all three cases for table, so we fit use am any time!'

z-m-09-03.thinking.1: Find a case where rule fail (counterexample) yourself

z-m-09-03.s.s1.o.a: Correct. E correct for all three cases, so e fit use any time any day

z-m-09-03.s.s1.o.b: No. E correct only in afternoon, no be morning
z-m-09-03.s.s1.r.b: Table get 10 a.m. and 8 a.m. correct too. Table no give reason to separate morning and afternoon.
z-m-09-03.s.s1.o.c: No. Even for this problem time difference fit change day by day, so we no fit use am
z-m-09-03.s.s1.r.c: Problem talk say Korea always 2 hours ahead. You change a condition wey don already set.
z-m-09-03.s.s1.o.d: Time like 1 a.m. for Korea need separate consideration
z-m-09-03.s.s1.r.d: Na thinking wey find one part wey dem never test whether rule hold for all times, then doubt am.
z-m-09-03.s.s1.explain: All three times for table dey during day or night wen date no change. If na early for Korea, near midnight, time wey 2 hours earlier fit dey previous day, so until you test those times e hard to say 'always'.
z-m-09-03.s.s2.prompt: Find Korea times wey Ayun method (time 2 hours earlier than Korea time) no work as e be. Write Korea times from 0 to 23 (1 a.m. na 1, 3 p.m. na 15). Find and enter all Korea times h wen Hanoi dey on the 'previous day'.

z-m-09-06.title: Input-output relation (rule multiplies and adds) 4 14 4 14
z-m-09-06.topic: Make several possible rules to show one input-output pair can't decide machine; narrow candidates with new data and explain how many tests needed.
z-m-09-06.goal: Secret number machine: input □, output △ = a×□+b. a natural at least 1, b natural 0 or more; no decimals/fractions. Input 4 gives 14.

z-m-09-06.s.s2.r.d: New data come, but you leave the possible rules the same by looking only at data wey dem already fit.
z-m-09-06.s.s2.o.e: None remain. No machine meet both results

z-m-09-06.s.s3.model.0: From the one result wen you put 4, (number multiplied, number added) fit be different pairs like 1 and 10, 2 and 6, 3 and 2, so we no fit decide. If two results come from different numbers, one pair become determined, so minimum na two.

z-m-09-07.title: 5 stamps for free drink: how many drinks you need buy?
z-m-09-07.topic: Connection between number bought and number received (stamp card)
z-m-09-07.goal: Notice say condition wey notice no specify fit change answer, calculate separately for each condition and write both answers.
z-m-09-07.material:
Cafe stamp card notice: 'We stamp 1 stamp each time you buy drink. Wen you collect 5 stamps, you get 1 free drink, and the 5 stamps disappear. No limit dey to how many times you fit get free drink, and you fit order through several separate orders.'
Hyeonu group wan drink 17 drinks altogether (bought and free drinks together) with new card wey get no stamps. 'Number of drinks to buy' mean buy as few as possible. Hyeonu calculate like this: 'If you buy 5 drinks, 1 free, so total 6 each time. For 17 drinks, buying 15 enough.'
